function.name: calculate_electric_current
function.description: Calculate the electric current through a conductor given voltage and resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

voltage.description: The voltage across the conductor in Volts. This is a float type value.

resistance.description: The resistance of the conductor in Ohms. This is a float type value.

conductance.description: The conductance of the conductor in Siemens. Optional if resistance is provided. Default: 0.3 This is a float type value.

message.content:
Electricity isn’t the discovery of a single individual—it’s a natural phenomenon that has been observed for millennia. Here’s a quick historical snapshot:

| Era | Key figure(s) | Contribution |
|-----|---------------|--------------|
| **Ancient Greece** | Thales of Miletus (c. 600 BCE) | Noted static electricity from rubbing amber. |
| **16th‑17th Century** | William Gilbert (1544–1603) | Coined “electricus” and studied magnetism vs. static charge. |
| **18th Century** | Benjamin Franklin (1706–1790) | Demonstrated lightning is electrical; introduced positive/negative charges. |
| **19th Century** | Alessandro Volta (1745–1827) | Invented the voltaic pile (first battery). |
| **Late 19th Century** | Michael Faraday (1791–1867) | Discovered electromagnetic induction. |

So while many scientists contributed to our understanding of electricity, it wasn’t “discovered” by one person alone.
